A declared state is unreachable from the trait's initial state via any transition path. BFS from the initial state over `transitions` (skipping `from == "*"` wildcards and the boot `INIT` self-loop on the initial state) never reaches it — dead topology. Surfaces only as a generic "uncovered" in the verifier today; caught here at author time. Worked example: std-booking-system ScheduleDisplay's `displaying`/`refreshing` cluster.

A trait-value literal (`<spec>.traits.<Trait>`) whose behavior or trait does not resolve against the installed behavior packages.
A `behavior/ref` whose argument is computed at run time: a behavior from data must arrive as a `behavior` value, never re-parsed from text.
An `["unquote", …]` call outside a quasiquote body in an `.orb` input.
Config field typed `slot` has a default value not in `VALID_SLOTS`
Config field typed `pattern` has a default value not in `PATTERN_TYPES`
Config field typed `secret` has a non-string default — the value is a credential REFERENCE (env-var key name), never secret material (I-29)

Config field typed `event` holds a value that is not a member of the trait's post-rename event set (SCAN-EVENT-KNOB-1). Definer-position knobs (A-UNIFY) skip this membership check — their value CREATES the event name — but still land here if the default isn't a plain string.
An event-typed config value addresses a trait the program does not have.
An event-typed config value addresses an event its trait does not declare as an external input.
A declared external input (`listens { EVENT -> external { … } }`) has no transition from the trait's initial state: inputs are complete commands.

Config field's default value doesn't match its declared structural shape (array vs scalar, object vs string, missing required, etc.). Fires after the typed-config carriers (`items` / `properties` / `values`) make the declared shape concrete enough to check against.

Config field uses `[object]` as its declared type. Banned because it lowers to an untyped `Array { inner: Json }` — the same shape the strict-lint floor catches as `Record<string, FieldValue | undefined>[]`. Authors should declare a named struct alias (e.g. `type FieldConfig = { name: string, label: string, ... }`) and use `[FieldConfig]` so the catalog + codegen carry real types.

A declaration uses a generic type — bare `json`, `object` (without declared `properties`), or `any` — in an entity field, config knob, type-alias member, or event payload field. Generic types are being eliminated from the language: renderable content belongs in `node`, structured data in inline `{ k: T }` shapes / named aliases / `Map K V`, and genuinely polymorphic atoms in declared type parameters. Hard error since 2026-09-01 (both behavior packages report zero occurrences).
A type reference names no declared type, entity or primitive
A type composition chain refers back to itself
Composed types do not share a kind (all Entity, all Trait, …)
A field is declared in more than one composed entity
A type body does not match its `::` type annotation
A type alias body uses a type parameter the alias does not declare
A type alias is applied with the wrong number of type arguments
An `emits` entry names a declared type that is not an Event type

A `node`-typed entity field receives a value the validator cannot statically check (a computed expression rather than a pattern-tree literal). Non-blocking: computed renderable content is legitimate, but its callback wiring is unchecked — prefer literal fragments (optionally via `let` bindings, which ARE resolved and checked).

A render-ui pattern literal is assigned to a field NOT typed `node` — renderable content hiding in a generic/structured field escapes every render-ui check. Type the field `node` (or `[node]`). Error severity.

Config field's `@tier "..."` annotation uses a value outside the allowed set. Allowed values: `essential`, `customization`, `advanced`, `internal`. Defense-in-depth — the parser allowlists the four values today; this L2 rule catches future regressions and any malformed `.orb` IR that bypasses the parser.

A trait imported from an atom carries a `linkedEntity` rebind, but the atom's binding is not marked `@rebindable`. The binding is fixed and the consumer may not redirect it. See `@rebindable` in `.lolo`.
A `@rebindable` rebind points at an entity that lacks fields the trait reads (its inferred `entityContract.requires`). The target would break the behavior.

A `linkedEntity` rebind names something that is not any orbital's primary or auxiliary entity anywhere in the schema — the §52 rebind-merge (`phases::inline::entity::merge_into_named_entity`) has nowhere to land the imported trait's fields. Retired 2026-09-19: this used to fall back to the caller's primary entity silently; it is now a hard error instead of a wrong-entity merge.

A `.lolo` event alias's `(E : Entity)` type parameter — lowered to the `"$E"` payload sentinel by `orbital-lolo` (increment 3-I, `docs/Almadar_LOLO.md` ~line 315/1387) — survived the inline phase's substitution pass because the trait carrying the sentinel has no `linkedEntity` to monomorphize it against. Fix: bind the trait to an entity (or, once explicit application ships, apply the alias with a concrete argument).

A call-site `events: { OLD: NEW }` rename names an OLD source key that does not exist in the imported trait's event set (its `emits[].event` ∪ `state_machine.transitions[].event`). The rename silently no-ops: nothing is renamed and the author's intent is lost. Surfaced from the inline phase where the imported trait's pre-rename event set is still visible.

A trait Reference's call-site `config` block supplies a key that matches no declared config knob on the referenced trait — the override silently no-ops (e.g. a stale `entity=` left over from a generator regression, or a knob the atom never declared).

A trait Reference's call site omits a key for a knob the referenced trait declares `!` (required). Any value form (literal, `@config.X` forward, `@entity.*`, payload ref) satisfies the requirement — only a fully missing key fires. The atom's own page binding is exempt.

A `local` trait's transitions contain a server-bound effect (`fetch`/`persist`/`call-service`/`ref`/`deref`/`swap`/`watch`/ `atomic`/`fetch-stream`), or a guard reading `@user.*`. `local` declares client-only dispatch (`OirTrait::dispatch_mode`) — a trait that actually touches the server or reads viewer identity is mis-tagged; its transitions would never await the round trip they depend on. Wave 2. Error severity.

A tick that runs in the browser (its trait is not server-awaited; the tick is not `[background]`) carries a server effect — a server-owned data effect, or a `runsOn: server` operator. Nothing replays a tick on the server, so the effect would be dropped. Server work goes through an emitted event a server-side trait handles.

`local` on a trait whose linked entity is neither `[shared]` nor `[runtime]`. `local` is only legal on an entity multiple traits co-mutate client-side (`[shared]`) or one that is never persisted at all (`[runtime]`) — on an ordinary persistent entity it would silently hide server-gated writes behind client-only dispatch. Wave 2. Error severity.

A transition guard reads `@user.*` while the trait's `OirTrait::dispatch_mode()` is `RuntimeOptimistic` or `HybridClientOnly` — evaluated client-side only. An identity check that never reaches the server is not an authorization boundary: the client can construct any `@user` value it likes. Wave 2. Warning severity (the guard may still be a legitimate UX precondition; it is never a security boundary).

A declared inline page is not the target of any `navigate` effect, any literal `href` value, and is not the root page or a parameterized page — nothing in the schema can ever route a viewer to it. Ported from the JS wiring lint's `page-absent-from-nav`, generalised: no navItems-array opt-in gate, and scalar `href` values count (not only object-array entries).

A page's content owner (`page_content_owner`'s `channel`/`ambiguous`) leaves a SECOND page-declared, inline, content-main-writing trait unclaimed: not an owner itself, not embedded by any client-bound trait, and not kin to the owner through either the config-channel or embed-containment relation (`reduce_to_owners({owner, this}).len() == 1` would mean related, not a rival). Two content bodies stacking into one page's `main`. Ported from the JS wiring lint's `unclaimed-main-writer` (warning there; error here per the owner's Q3 ruling).

A page whose `main` a shell owns through a config channel (`contentTrait` …) also mounts a trait that paints a control into `main` which neither the owner nor anything it embeds references: the control stacks outside the shell's layout instead of inside it.

A composed trait (`sourceBehavior` set) has a state no event the program can produce leads to: every transition into it waits on an event nothing routes in, no control or effect fires, and the host is not declared to send (`external`). An atom's own inputs are its offer; a composition that never wires one leaves that part of it dead.

A composed trait (`sourceBehavior` set) has a live transition, from a reachable state, on an event the program cannot produce under its resolved config: no listens route, control or effect fires it, it is not a lifecycle event and not declared `external` (G-CROSS-144).

A composed trait's rendered control fires an event carrying a value that no other trait hears and whose own handling reads none of it: the value the user entered is discarded (a form submission nothing keeps).

A page whose content owner is ambiguous: two or more page-declared `main` writers, none composing the others, no shell channel naming one. Renders stacked alone, but any shell that designates one `contentTrait` turns the rest into second bodies (G-ORB-128).

Multiple traits rendering to same slot in a reachable post-INIT state (emitted as a warning; INIT-state case still errors via `SlotContention`)

Prop value type doesn't match expected type from registry

L2.1 keystone: render-ui prop bound to a `@payload.X` / `@entity.X` / `@config.X` / SExpression operator whose resolved type doesn't match any of the prop's declared `types` in the patterns registry. Distinct from `RenderUIPropTypeMismatch` (literal-only); this rule uses the F3 binding resolver to walk through bindings and SExpression operator return types (sharpened by F2's `returnSemantics` for input-dependent operators). Gap #6 in `docs/Almadar_Std_Verification.md`.

L2.4: render-ui binds an array literal to a prop whose pattern declares per-element required fields (`items.properties.<field>.required`), and one or more elements omit a required field. Catches the landing-page/about-page/showcase class of bugs where the lolo `[StepCard]` type omits `id` but the consuming `step-flow-organism` pattern requires it — surfaced at codegen as TS2322 before this rule. Walks `OirValue::Array` element-by-element against `items.properties` from `patterns-registry.json`. Discovery context: `docs/Almadar_Std_Gaps.md` §13.

Entity name collides with a sibling trait's generated `<TraitName>State` or `<TraitName>Event` union type. The TS codegen emits both `import type { <EntityName> } from '@app/shared'` and `type <TraitName>State = '...'` / `type <TraitName>Event = '...'` in every server-handler / client-hook / view file — when the entity name equals one of those generated unions, the import collides with the local declaration and tsc raises TS2440 "Import declaration conflicts with local declaration".  Defense-in-depth pair with the lolo lowering check `LowerError::EntityNameShadowsTraitUnion`: the lolo rule catches hand-authored `.lolo`, this validator rule catches `.orb` mutated directly by an agent or factory that bypassed the lolo parse path. Convention fix: rename the entity (e.g. `<TraitName>Data`).

L2.2: render-ui prop with `kind: "event-ref"` or `kind: "callback"` bound to an event-name string whose declared payload schema in the trait's `emits {}` block doesn't match the component's documented bus emit shape (registry's `emitPayloadSchema` for event-ref props; `callbackArgs` for callback props). Gap #32 in `docs/Almadar_Std_Verification.md`.

L2.3: render-ui pattern carries a string literal that matches an event name no longer in the trait's event set after the inline phase applies an `events: { OLD: NEW }` override. Detects the stale literal that the compiler's events-rewrite pass should have rewritten — defense-in-depth for C1 (the compiler fix). Gap #30 in `docs/Almadar_Std_Verification.md`.

`notify` is sugar for `render-ui toast { type: alert, … }`, desugared at `.lolo` lowering (owner ruling 2026-09-11) — the `.orb` IR never carries a `notify` effect kind. A `notify` tuple reaching L2 means a hand-authored `.orb` or a registry not yet re-emitted.

Navigate effect references a path that doesn't resolve to any declared `pages[].path` across the resolved schema. Post-inline backstop for L1.2 — catches navigate calls injected by molecule- level `effects: { ... }` overrides AND navigate calls that targeted imported pages from `uses` refs that L1 couldn't see.

Trait declares an event in its `emits[]` block but no transition fires it via `(emit X)` or operator emit-config success/failure. Usually a copy-paste leftover or a stale declaration after a rename; gap #2 defense in `docs/Almadar_Std_Verification.md`.
`orb validate --final`: a rendered control fires an event no trait handles — not the rendering trait, an embedder of it, nor a `listens` route (G-ORB-187).

`emits { @config.<knob> -> ... }` references a knob that isn't a DECLARED string-typed config field with a default (Option B contract). Left unresolved by the inline phase; surfaces here with the specific clause that failed.

`program/eval` carries no `emit.failure` event: the validator's errors come back through the failure arm, so without one they are dropped.

Operator declares `requiresEmitSuccess: true` in canonical-operators.json but the effect call site is missing the trailing options object or its `emit.success` event key. Applies to fetch / persist / call-service / ref by default; any future operator can opt in via the same JSON flag.
A success event only `(fetch X { id: … })` produces declares `data` as a list; a by-id fetch delivers one row (G-ORB-185).
A `fetch` option outside its closed enum (`deliver: rows | ids`, `total: exact | none`).
`deliver: ids` makes the success event's `data` a row-set reference; any use other than passing it whole as a `render-ui` prop value reads rows that were never delivered.
`deliver: ids` with `include`: included relations are row content.
`deliver: ids` with no `emit.success`: the reference is only ever passed whole to a `render-ui` prop, and nothing can reference a result that no event carries.
`total: none` skips the count, so the success event's `totalCount` is never set.

A trait emits an event (an `(emit …)` effect or an operator emit-config result) that a SIBLING trait in the same orbital has an arm for, but no declared `listens` route delivers it from that emitter. Events reach another trait only through declared routes, so the intent terminates in nothing (std-pong's PADDLE_MOVE, 2026-09-24).

A trait writing a client-held `[runtime]` frame from client ticks (or bound to a `[shared]` one another trait ticks) is not `local`: its dispatches post to a stateful host whose stale copy folds back.

Payload mismatch between emitter and listener

`listens` references a source trait or event that doesn't exist in the resolved IR. Defense-in-depth backstop for the L1 (`orbital-lolo`) `LowerError::ListenSourceUnresolved` check; surfaces the same defect after `use`-imports inline so atoms/molecules pulled into an orbital can't accidentally introduce dangling listens.

A `listens { S.E -> TRIGGER }` route whose source trait S DOES declare event E in its `emits[]` contract, but nothing in the schema currently produces E live — no effect emit, no rendered `action:`/ event prop, no structured `itemActions` entry, and no trait embedded (directly or transitively) inside S produces it either. The contract permits it; a config override (an itemActions/browseItemActions narrowed at this call site, say) removed the only producer, so the route is a live wire with nothing behind it — fires whatever the emit's declared `scope` is (`external` included: a cross-orbital broadcast still needs a live broadcaster). Ported from the JS wiring lint's `listener-affordance-removed-by-config`.

A `listens { Src.EVENT -> TRIGGER }` entry names an internal TRIGGER that no transition in the SAME trait reacts to. The bus would deliver the event but the state machine has no handler — the wire silently drops. Runs post-inline so the `events: { OLD: NEW }`-rename variant (where the rewrite renamed the transition event but the listen trigger drifted) is caught too. Defense-in-depth for the L1 (`orbital-lolo`) author-time check on hand-authored `.lolo`.
Composing trait's override map touches an event declared `scope: 'internal'`. Error severity. See COMP-7 in docs/Almadar_Agent_Behaviors_Plan.md.

A `fetch`'s `filter` compares a LITERAL `(object/get @entity <field>)` against a value, but no `persist create`/`update` anywhere in the schema (own trait, sibling trait, or a `persistent:`-collection-mate entity) ever supplies that field — the filter can never match a real row. Cross-orbital because the persistor routinely lives in a sibling orbital (the modal + persistor idiom). `[identity]`-roster entities and `@intrinsic` fields are exempt; a declared default only exempts the field when it folds, under the trait's resolved config, to the SAME literal the filter's comparand folds to — an undecidable (payload/entity/user-bound) comparand stays silent rather than guessing. Ported from `filter-field-never-written`. Error severity.

A `type: 'relation'` field's `relation.entity` does not resolve to any entity declared in the same schema. Error severity; the entity-scope validator also emits `ORB_E_INVALID_RELATION` for the same condition. See COMP-9 in docs/Almadar_Agent_Behaviors_Plan.md.

A pattern prop tagged `kind: 'field-ref'` (scalar) or `itemKind: 'field-ref'` (array element) carries a value that does not resolve to any field on the linked entity. Error severity. See Phase 3.2/3.3 in docs/Almadar_Agent_Behaviors_Plan.md.

A `listens { Src.EVENT -> TRIGGER }` route's TRIGGER declares a required leaf payload field the route never produces: no `with { }` mapping supplies it, and (pass-through, no mapping) the source trait's declared `emits { EVENT { ... } }` contract never declares it at the same dotted path either. The consumer's transition reads `?payload.<field>` as `undefined` at runtime.

A host trait's `listens { Child.EV -> EV }` route where `Child` is a trait the host embeds (directly or transitively), `EV` is fired by a control inside `Child`'s subtree, and the host already has a transition on `EV`. The control's emit bubbles to every scope on the embed chain, so the host already hears it directly; the route is a second delivery of the same physical event.
A `*.EVENT` route on an event whose payload carries a `CallKey`-typed `key`, with a guard that never reads it.
Binding has invalid format
Unknown binding root
`@config.<key>` literal whose key no reachable config schema declares
Invalid binding path
@state binding should not have path
@now binding should not have path
@payload not available in tick context
`@event`/`@prevEvents`/`@prevStates`/`@fromState`/`@toState` in a tick, which has no delivery
`@fromEntity` (the row before a transition) outside an `@ensures`
`@fromState`/`@toState`/`@prevStates`/`@prevEvents` written with a path
`@event.<path>` that does not follow the `{ event, payload, source }` record
Unknown entity in @EntityName binding
Invalid field name in binding path
Set target missing field path
@payload.field references a field not declared in event payload schema

@payload.field is declared but its type does not match the operator argument or comparison it appears in (e.g. string used where a number was expected). Warn-only in V2 Phase 0 rollout; escalates to error in the Phase 5 cleanup. Wired up in a follow-up pass over operator signatures; the class is declared here so the code path can reference it and emit warnings incrementally.

`(set @entity.X ?payloadField)` writes a payload field whose declared type does not match the target entity field's declared type. The lolo crate catches this at author time for `.lolo`; this is the raw-`.orb` defense-in-depth backstop. Payload field types are sourced from the trait's `emits[].payload_schema` and `listens` payload metadata.

`(set @entity.X literal)` assigns a string literal that is not a member of the target field's declared enum (`values: [...]`). The declared union was previously validated + emitted but never enforced — an out-of-set value passed silently. The lolo crate catches this at author time for `.lolo`; this is the raw-`.orb` defense-in-depth backstop.

`(set @entity.X (op …))` assigns an operator/expression value whose inferred result type is incompatible with the target field's declared type (e.g. `(set @entity.count (str/concat …))` into a `number` field). The value's type is inferred *through* the S-expression via the canonical operator `return_semantics` lattice; an unknowable result (`Json`) never rejects (Gap G-LOLO-SET-OP-RETURN).

An ordering comparison (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) whose operands infer to a number on one side and a string on the other. The JS runtime coerces, the compiled TypeScript does not typecheck, and Rust compares kinds — the paths disagree. Convert one side so both are the same kind.

An operator argument whose static type contradicts the type the operator table declares for its position — `(str/upper @entity.count)` with `count: number`, `(+ "a" 1)`. Both evaluators raise the same typed mismatch at run time (D-12), so the program can never do what it says.

A value handed to an operator's type variable has no determined type — an unresolved expression, an expression value, json, a list whose items share no type — so what the variable stands for, and the type of the call's result, is unknown. There are no generic types: give the value a real type (a declared payload or entity shape, a named union alias for a list of differently-shaped items).

An ordering comparison (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) over an operand that can be missing or null — an optional entity field with no default, an optional payload field — that the program neither guards with a presence check (`(and (validate/required x) (< x 3))`, an `if`/`when` on presence) nor declares a default for. Both evaluators read a missing value as below any number; every push-down store fails the comparison, so the meaning is the program's to state.

An operand that can be missing or null — an optional entity field with no default, an optional payload field — handed to a position the kernel raises on when it is null (`rejectsNull` in the operator table), with no presence check or default in front of it. The program says what a missing value means: a guard, a default, or a required field.

`(set @entity.X @config.<knob>)` where the value is STILL the literal `@config.<knob>` token post-inline (no default resolved it, no call-site override supplied one) and `X` is a REQUIRED entity field. The emitter has nothing honest to assign — a required TS slot gets `undefined`. Give the knob a default or make the field optional.
`(emit EVT {...})` literal payload is missing a field the event's declared payload marks as required. Error severity.
`(emit EVT {...})` literal carries a field that is not declared on the event's payload schema. Error severity.
`(emit EVT {...})` literal provides a value whose primitive type does not match the declared `PayloadField.field_type`. Error severity.

The whole `@user` record fills a required slot (an emit payload `X!`, a required entity field) with no guard on its presence: a dispatch with no viewer (an os/ completion, a tick) has a null `@user`. Error severity.
An `emit` repeats an earlier one of the same transition identically: the dispatch loop collapses the second.

An event/emit `payloadSchema` field name is not a valid TypeScript identifier (contains a dot, space, or leading digit). Codegen turns each field into a struct member, so `row.category` would emit broken TS. Validate-layer defense-in-depth for the lowering pass that flattens nested payload field names. Error severity.
An array field (entity or payload-schema) declares no element type.

A render-ui pattern prop typed `EntityWith<K>` declares required entity fields (`requiredFields` in the registry), but the bound entity does not provide them and no remap/field-map supplies them. The component would render blank rows. Remap-aware (runs post-inline). Error severity.

**RETIRED (2026-08-30) — superseded by `EmitPayloadNotProduced`, which checks the full shape rather than only the empty-payload case.** No longer raised anywhere; the variant is kept so external tooling matching on the wire string `ORB_EMIT_SUCCESS_PAYLOAD_RETURN_MISMATCH` does not break on an unknown code.  `emit: { success: "X" }` config on a data operator declares success event X but X's declared payload does not match the operator's `effect.produces` at this call site. Warn-only.

**The payload invariant.** An event's declared payload type IS its access path: declaring `Survey` means the payload is the row (read `?name`); declaring `{ row : Survey }` means read `?row.name`. This fires when an event declares a field that the effect firing it does not actually emit — so every read of that field is `undefined` at runtime, even though `orb validate` and `orb verify` otherwise pass. Checked as width subtyping (`declared ⊆ produced`): declaring FEWER fields than are emitted is legal, declaring one that is never emitted is not. Replaces the narrower `EmitSuccessPayloadWrapped` (persist-only) and `EmitSuccessPayloadReturnMismatch` (empty-payload-only) checks. Error severity.

**RETIRED (2026-08-30) — superseded by `EmitPayloadNotProduced`.** This check only recognised a wrapper on `persist create`/`update` whose type named that exact entity; the general rule catches the same defect at any operator and in shapes this one was blind to (a wrapper naming a different entity, a field the operator never emits at all). Kept so external tooling matching `ORB_EMIT_SUCCESS_PAYLOAD_WRAPPED` still resolves.  A `persist create`/`persist update` call's `emit: { success: "X" }` names an event X whose declared payload wraps the persisted entity under a single field (`type X = Event { row: EntityName }`), but `persist create`/`update` emits the persisted row directly (flat, unwrapped) on success in both @almadar/runtime and orbital-core — verified live 2026-08-30 (std-thread's `ThreadPostCreated`): a wrapped declaration validates and compiles clean but every `?row.<field>` read silently returns undefined at runtime. Warn-only.

Phase F.2: two or more traits declare the same external event name in their `emits` arrays but disagree on the declared payload field list. Consumers that listen on the event will see one shape from one emitter and a different shape from another. Error severity.
Two traits of one program carry the same trait id; listens match sources by id, so each hears the other's emits.
@entity.field references a field not present on the linked entity

@entity.field is referenced by render-ui / guard / effect but no transition in the same trait runs `(set @entity.field <value>)`. Per the explicit-binding rule, every `@entity.X` read must be backed by at least one explicit setter; otherwise the value is undefined and the component renders empty. Surfaces post-inline so atoms imported via `uses` get checked too. Defense-in-depth backstop for the L1 `LowerError::EntityFieldNeverSet` check.

`(persist update|delete <Entity> @entity)` passes the WHOLE row, so the row key never appears as an `@entity.id` read and `BindingEntityFieldNeverSet` cannot see it. An unbound `id` resolves empty and the runtime refuses the write outright.

A transition writes `@entity.F` (or its whole row) and renders an embedded trait (`@trait.X`, incl. a hoisted inline `<A.traits.T/>`) whose call-site value reads that field of the same PERSISTENT entity. The embed resolves `@entity` against its own frame at its own render (its mount), so it shows the value from before this transition. Read the value the transition used instead (a call-site capture, `?row.F`), or route the host event to the embed's INIT.

`persist create E { ... }` with an explicit data literal whose key set lacks a field that `E.@create` compares (e.g. `@create sender == @user.id` and the literal has no `sender`). The access policy will never be satisfied by a row this transition itself creates — every future `@update`/`@delete`/`@read` gated on that field locks the creator out of their own row. A bare `persist create @entity` (whole frame) is not a hit. Wave 2. Error severity.

`persist create E { id: "literal", … }`: the row names a string-literal id, so the second run creates a row that already exists and fails with `duplicate-id`. A seed or singleton re-save is an authored `persist upsert` (create-or-replace by id). Error severity.

`persist delete E <expression>` / `persist update E <expression> data`: the single forms take the row id as a binding path or a literal, so an expression resolves no row key at run time. Error severity.
`persist … { where: … }`: the guard is a one-param `fn` over the stored row that never reads the frame (`@entity`), on a single `delete` or `update` only (EXEC-STEP-8). Error severity.
An effect (`emit`, `persist`, `set`, `notify`, …) inside the `fn` body of a collection operator: a lambda is evaluated for its value, an effect there never runs. Error severity.
`@trait` binding with no trait name — bare `@trait` is not resolvable.
`@trait.X` trait name doesn't match the `PascalCase` identifier pattern.
`@trait.X` references a trait not declared in the current orbital.
A trait's render-ui references itself via `@trait.<self>`.
Cycle detected in the `@trait.X` reference graph (e.g. A → B → A).
`@trait.X` appears outside a `children:` array or a `node`-typed pattern prop — valid positions are where a subtree can be substituted.

`@trait.X` (a render-only, client-side binding) appears outside a `render-ui` effect entirely — in a guard, a non-render effect (`fetch`/`set`/`persist`/`ref`/`call-service`), or a tick. Trait references are render-time composition primitives and have no meaning in data/effects/control flow.

A render-ui payload embeds `@config.<knob>` (as a child or inside a `children` entry) where `<knob>` is a `trait`-typed config field whose resolved value is `none` (unbound), and the render-ui is not guarded by an `(if @config.<knob> ...)` wrapping it in the same effect list. An unbound trait knob's embed renders nothing — the closed-circuit rule that no wire may terminate in nothing (owner ruling 2026-09-13: a `trait`-typed config knob may be `none`).
A render-ui payload embeds an `orbital`-typed field: an orbital value is data (an import body) and never renders — only trait values embed.
A bridged embed delivers an event nothing in the program sends.
A bridged embed re-emits an event nothing in the program handles.

A non-`[shared]`, `Runtime`-persistence entity is mutated (via `set` or a tick write) by ≥2 distinct traits. Each mutator gets an isolated per-trait copy, so if one of the mutators' render-ui also reads the entity, it only ever sees its own trait's writes — never the others'. Error severity: add `[shared]` to the entity, or isolate the mutators.

A `[shared]` entity has ≥2 distinct traits writing the SAME field. Coupled mechanics writing one field must be one ordered pipeline, not parallel writers — undefined last-write-wins ordering otherwise.
A `[shared]` entity is render-ui-read by more than one distinct trait. Exactly one render authority is allowed per shared entity, mirroring `SlotContention`'s single-owner rule.

Post-inline: an entity field carrying `mergedFrom` (added by the rebind-merge auto-merge, `merge_imported_entity_fields`) that no trait of the consuming orbital reads, writes, fetch-includes, or persists — R-ENTITY-FIELD-UNION-ACROSS-SAME-NAMED-ENTITY. The merge already narrows to referenced fields at compose time; this catches drift when a later edit removes the trait/effect that used to justify the merge. Error severity.
A trait runs a non-`Cron` tick (frame/duration interval) against a `Persistent` linked entity. Corpus-facing backstop mirroring the lolo L1 tick guards. Error severity.

A non-`Cron` tick effect calls a server-async operator (the canonical registry's `std-agent` category — `agent/generate`, `agent/invoke`, etc.). Repeated per-tick LLM/agent calls can pile up faster than they resolve. Error severity.

An explicit `persist create`/`persist update` data LITERAL (an `OirExpr::Object`, never a bare whole-frame `@entity`) names an `@intrinsic` field of the target entity. Intrinsic fields are trait-owned view-state/machinery (`OirEntity::frame_fields`'s ONLY allow-list) — never a persisted column — so writing one into the database is a category error the author almost certainly meant as a domain field. Wave 2. Error severity.

An `@intrinsic` field is used as an AUTHORIZATION input: it appears in an access policy (`@create`/`@read`/`@update`/`@delete`), or in a transition guard that also reads `@user.*`/role/identity AND the transition performs `persist`/`call-service`. Intrinsic fields are trait-computed view-state the runtime never seeds or persists — using one to gate a mutation means the gate is trivially bypassable (the caller controls the "intrinsic" value directly). A plain precondition guard with no identity comparison is not a hit. Wave 2. Error severity.

`(set @entity.<f> ...)` writes a non-`@intrinsic` column of a `[persistent]` entity in a transition with no row binding (no `id`/`?row`-bearing event payload, no `entityId` in scope) AND the owning trait never runs `persist create`/`persist update` on that entity anywhere — so the write can never land: it is not framed to an identified row, and nothing ever persists it. A draft form that sets columns across several transitions before a final `persist create` is legitimate (the write eventually lands); this only fires when the trait has no landing transition at all. Wave 2. Error severity.

Same event emitted multiple times in same context

State has no incoming transitions
State has no outgoing transitions
Action-component mismatch
Overlay slot (modal/drawer) missing exit transition
Modal-to-inline transition missing render-ui("main", ...) alongside render-ui("modal", null)
Render-ui handler fires event with no matching transition from the rendering state

A rendered affordance's event-bearing prop (`action`, `itemActions[].event`, `submitEvent`, `onChange`, …) targets a lifecycle event (`orbital_core::events::BUS_EXCLUDED_EVENTS`). The bus never re-delivers `INIT`/`LOAD`/`$MOUNT`, so the control is dead on click.

A transition's effects (`fetch`/`persist`/`call-service`) declare an `emit.failure` event, but no arm at the destination state (`from === to || from === '*'`) handles it — the async result contract's failure half is a live wire terminating in nothing. Ported from the JS wiring lint's `failure-arm-missing` (client-bound traits only). Error severity.

The failure-handling arm found for [`CircuitFailureArmMissing`]'s contract exists but paints nothing (no `render-ui <slot> <non-null>` anywhere in its effects, including through `if`/`do`) — the failure is caught but never shown to the user. A trait declared `[integration]` is headless, so its arm also handles the failure by emitting an event some trait in the program listens to, or one it declares `-> external`; an emit nobody hears still reports. Ported from `failure-arm-renders- nothing`. Error severity.

A transition renders a non-self-overlaying pattern into an overlay slot (`modal`/`drawer`/`overlay`), but the destination state has no `CLOSE`/`CANCEL` arm — the generic portal shell's own dismiss control (X / Escape / overlay-click) fires an event nothing handles. Ported from `modal-shell-close-deaf`. Error severity.

A transition renders a SELF-overlaying pattern (`slideOver: true` anywhere in the payload tree) into an overlay slot — the generic portal shell wraps it too, producing two stacked overlay chromes. Ported from `self-overlay-inside-modal-shell`. Error severity.

A transition's own effects list contains a top-level `(emit <event>)` naming a lifecycle event (`orbital_core::events::BUS_EXCLUDED_EVENTS`) — the bus never re-delivers it, so this half of the closed circuit is written but can never run. Sibling production site to [`RenderActionLifecycleEvent`](ErrorCode::RenderActionLifecycleEvent) (an explicit effect instead of a rendered affordance prop). Ported from the JS wiring lint's `dead-lifecycle-emit`. Error severity.

A transition arm re-emits its OWN trigger event (`X --X--> Y` whose effects contain `(emit X ...)`), the `to` state has another arm on X, and the re-emitted payload does not derive from `@payload` — the runtime path re-enters an arm on the same event with unchanged payload and loops forever (G-RUNTIME-020). Payloads derived from `@payload` (sentinel fan-out counters) make progress per hop and are not flagged; neither is a self-emit whose target state has no same-event arm (a dead-end broadcast). Error severity.

An inline trait owns a non-empty `stateMachine.transitions` but is absent from `client_bound_traits(orbital)` — no page declares it and no page's `@trait.X` embed closure reaches it, so the client never mounts a state machine for it and it can never handle an event in the shipped app. Ported from the JS wiring lint's `client-unbound-state-machine`. Error severity.
A page trait that initializes on `INIT` has a reachable state with no `INIT` arm: trait state survives unmount, so revisiting the page from that state does nothing (G-ORB-186).

A transition moves `from -> to` (not a self-transition) with NO effects at all, out of a `from` state some OTHER arm already painted into a main slot (`orbital_core::slots::MAIN_SLOTS`) — the machine leaves that state but the screen keeps its old paint standing, so every affordance routed here is dead. Client-bound gated (an unbound trait's arms never run in the shipped client at all). Ported from the JS wiring lint's `dead-bodiless-action`. Error severity.

A state-CHANGING transition (`from != to`) whose `fetch`/`persist` effects declare async-result events (`collect_async_result_events`: EVERY value of the `emit` map, recursing through `if`/`do`) that the destination state's own arms (`from === to-state || from === "*"`) don't handle — the requester departs before it can hear its own operation's result, so the cascade lands on a machine deaf to it and wedges. NOT client-bound gated (the JS predicate has none here, unlike its `failure-arm-missing` sibling). Ported from the JS wiring lint's `async-result-deaf-target` (warning there; error here per the 0/0 ruling). Error severity.

The trait that OWNS a page's content region (`page_content_owner`'s `channel`/`sole-writer`) has a user-triggered arm that repaints its own main-slot body with something offering no way on: no content-body pattern, no registry event-kind prop bound to a live (non-lifecycle) event or an unresolved binding, and no `@trait.X` embed. "User- triggered" means the event is reachable from a rendered affordance or a `listens` route, transitively, minus async-result and lifecycle events. Exempt: an arm running its own `fetch`/`persist` (its result arm repaints); a non-self-transition escaping to a state with another producible, non-lifecycle arm. Ported from the JS wiring lint's `viewer-stranded`, predicate revised 2026-09-12 per the F31 live probe (`play_scene` on `ui-minigolf-board`/`std-chem-titration`): the JS's labelled-control test and `@`/`?` sigil branch were both heuristics and are dropped — a registry event-kind prop is the only test. Error severity.

Icon name is empty
Icon may not exist in Lucide

A `time/*` operator was given a unit literal outside the vocabulary. Unchecked, it throws at evaluation time — and inside a read predicate that means rows are dropped fail-closed while the run still reports PASS (`S-CALENDAR-RANGE-FILTER-USES-UNSUPPORTED-TIME-UNITS`).
Query singleton missing search field
Query singleton missing recommended fields
Pattern doesn't support query prop
Query references unknown singleton
Query singleton is unused
Event emitted but not declared in trait.emits
Event name not UPPER_SNAKE_CASE
Tick emits undeclared event
Listener scope mismatch
External emit missing payload definition
Schema missing name
Schema has no orbitals
Schema version is empty

More than one differently-named `[identity]` entity in one composed program. `@user` is a single root resolving to a single viewer, so two declarations make every `@user.x` ambiguous. (Same-name duplicates are already rejected upstream by `validate_entity_uniqueness`.)

A literal compared against an `@user.<field>` whose declared type is a closed vocabulary is not one of that vocabulary's members — a branch that can never be taken. The bug class that let std-healthcare's `"patient"` and std-lms's `"student"` ship green.
`@user.<field>` names a field the declared `[identity]` entity does not have. Resolves to null at runtime, so the guard silently takes its negative branch.
`@entity.<field>` (or `(object/get @entity field)`) inside an `@read`/`@create`/`@update`/`@delete` directive names a field the OWNING entity does not have.

An access directive compares an `@entity.<field>` against `@user.id`, but `<field>` is not a relation to the `[identity]` entity. The comparison is then between a free-text scalar and a roster id — it type-checks, reads like ownership, and matches nothing, because the seeder only stamps viewer ids onto DECLARED relations. This is the `customerEmail` trap: a policy that silently denies everyone while looking correct.

An entity declares ≥1 owner column (a declared relation to the `[identity]` entity, via `owner_fields_from_schema` — never by field name) but no `read_policy` and no stated `access_waivers.read` reason. An undeclared policy is ALLOW-ALL, not deny-all, so every viewer reads every row. L3 port of JS `unscoped-owned-entity`.
`store: X` (entity or app header) names no orbital of the program (EXEC-STORE-4). Error severity.
A store driver orbital has no trait handling one of ROW_READ / ROW_LIST / ROWS_QUERY / ROWS_WRITE (`spec/store/row-store.lolo`). Error severity.
`store:` on an entity whose rows live in no store (`[runtime]` or browser-`local`). Error severity.
A trait outside a store driver orbital emits a row verb: the store seam alone asks a driver, one frame per ask (EXEC-STORE-4). Error severity.
A single `persist delete|update` on an entity whose driver declares `writeCapabilities.conditional` false: the take is one conditional op (EXEC-STEP-8). Error severity.

A trait's `config.groupByField` + `config.columns[].key` bucket rows of the linked entity by strict key equality, but the field's declared enum allows a value no column key names — those rows match no column and silently disappear. L3 port of JS `groupby-enum-column-gap`.

A trait embedded via `@trait.X` by ≥2 referrers that itself declares an `@config.<key>` forward. One declaration serves one embedder (its forwards chain to the first referrer only), so the second embedder's call-site config never takes effect. L3 port of JS `embedded-sibling-single-referrer`.

A trait pins `config.theme` to a non-empty literal that isn't a binding (`@…`) and doesn't match the schema's app-level `theme` declaration. `""` and bindings are unpinned — an orbital riding the ambient default is silent. L3 port of the app-level branch of JS `app-theme-divergent`; the dominant-vote branch is a name/plurality heuristic and is retired, not ported.
A `data-theme` resolves to a literal theme the program does not declare (app or orbital `theme`, or the app's `themes`), so the compiled client ships no stylesheet for it (G-UI-106).
An access directive reads a binding root other than `@entity`/`@user` — the directive has no call site, so `@payload`/`@config`/`@state` are not meaningful there.

An access directive reads `@user` in a program declaring no `[identity]` entity. Unlike a bare pre-existing `@user` read (which falls back to the implicit default shape), a NEW authorization construct must have a real roster — that is what makes personas switchable.

Two entity declarations bind the same `persistent:` collection and declare DIFFERENT access directives. One table cannot honestly have two visibility rules, and the runtime's collection-level inheritance has no principled way to choose (`R-SHADOW-ENTITY-SHARES-COLLECTION-DIRECTIVES-DONT-APPLY`).

Compose link-check: an orbital's `expects entity X` / `expects entity X [identity]` names a requirement no orbital in the program provides. The message names WHO ASKED — the consumer orbital — so the repair is attributable.
Compose link-check: the named provider entity exists but lacks the expected kind (e.g. `expects entity Customer [identity]` where `Customer` carries no `[identity]` tag).
Compose link-check: the provider entity declares no field with an expected shape name. Names consumer, provider, and field.

Compose link-check: the provider has the expected field but with an incompatible type (per orbital-core's `type_compat`; literal unions use subset semantics — every expected member must be a provider member).

Standalone AND compose self-consistency: the consumer uses a field it did not declare — an `@user.<field>` read outside its `expects identity` shape, or a `persist` payload field outside its `expects entity` shape. The consumer's declaration is its own source of truth.
A spec proposition (`@invariant` on `expects entity`, `@holds` on an `expects trait` state) is broken: a write or transition of the program falsifies it on a counterexample the evaluator confirms.
A spec proposition the prover could not decide (an expression outside the decidable fragment, or a write whose effect on the proposition is over-approximated). Never a pass.
A `uses A from "…" { config { … } }` call-site override names a key the imported behavior's app-level `config {}` (`OrbitalSchema.config`, `Almadar_Orbital_Import.md` §4.5) does not declare.

L2 twin of `orbital-lolo`'s `LowerError::SharedEntityWithoutPersistenceMode` (`ORB_S_SHARED_WITHOUT_PERSISTENCE_MODE`): `EntityDefinition.shared && persistence.is_none()` on the input schema. Nothing about a `[shared]` entity may be inferred — it must say `persistent: <collection>` or `runtime` explicitly. Catches a `.orb` mutated directly (factory edits, agent rewrites) that bypasses the `.lolo` parse path. Runs before any persistence defaulting. Wave 2. Error severity.
A populated dual-carry id field points at an id that is neither a node declared in the schema's arena (orbital/entity/trait/page/emit-event) nor a `schema.ledger` entry. The edge is dangling.
Both a reference's name field and its id sibling are populated, but the ledger's `curName` for that id disagrees with the name (dual-carry drift).
An id's kind prefix (`identity::id_kind_of`) disagrees with the reference position it occupies (e.g. an `ent_` id sitting in a trait `refId`).
A ledger row whose id no node in the schema carries — a stale row left behind after its node was removed. Error severity.

One event id is declared by two or more DIFFERENT traits in the same orbital (`stateMachine.events[].id` / `emits[].eventId`). Ids are the durable node keys of the identity graph; a shared id makes every id→name resolution (identity normalize, id-primary dispatch) ambiguous. Inline's event-id hygiene derives per-instance ids at expansion, so this fires only on an artifact produced outside that path.
A ledger-less `.orb` carries an authored declaration id that loading re-mints (`stamp::ensure_stamped`). Warning severity.
`<prefix>/<name>` names a prefix no installed behavior package declares.
The prefix resolved to an installed package, but it has no behavior by that name (or `std/behaviors/<name>` matched neither the std source nor any other installed package).
`std/behaviors/<name>` matched the same behavior name in two or more non-std installed packages.
Two different installed packages declare the same `orb.prefix`.
A behavior name is duplicated within or across installed package sources.
An installed behavior package's registry cannot be read or indexed.

Generic invalid reference format
Theme reference names a theme not in the valid set (built-in `@almadar-ui/themes/` registry ∪ orbital-declared inline themes)
